newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - April 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - April 29.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- LEEDS UNITED CHIEF TOLD TO QUIT TEAM

Robin Launders, chief executive of Leeds United, resigned yesterday. He was given a choice of resignation or dismissal at a meeting with the chairman of Caspian, the media group which bought Leeds last summer. It is understood that difficulties between Launders and the Caspian board over his manner of running the club were behind the meeting.
-- BRITISH POUND RISES ON EMU FEARS

The pound rose yesterday as investors opted for 'safe' currencies after weekend warnings from the International Monetary Fund over the dangers of upset in the European markets by possible delays to European monetary union. Expectations of an early rates rise after the election also helped boost demand for sterling.
-- ABBEY ACTS OVER RUSH FOR FIXED MORTGAGES

Demand for fixed rate mortgages is strong as fears grow of an interest rates rise after the election. Abbey National announced yesterday it was withdrawing its current fixed rate mortgage offer as a direct result of demand. It said it would withdraw the 6.99 percent rate at the close of today's business.
THE TIMES
-- SEARS TO DETAIL STRONG EXIT AND SELL-OFF

Sears will announce on Tuesday a plan to demerge its Selfridges department store business. Details of the departure of chief executive Liam Strong will also be announced, with a 500,000 stg payoff likely when he leaves in June.
-- UNIT TRUST PEP SALES SET 1.1 BILLION STG RECORD IN MARCH

Personal equity plan sales rose in March to 1.1 billion stg, a record for any month, in a last-minute rush to beat the taxman. Unit trust Pep sales in the latest tax year exceeded 6.2 billion stg, a rise of 43 percent on the previous year.
-- MULCAHY PAY TOPS ONE MILLION STG AT KINGFISHER

Sir Geoffrey Mulcahy, chief executive at Kingfisher, saw his pay rise above one million stg last year to a total of 1.266 million stg. The group, which owns Woolworths, B&Q and Comet, saw good trading and profits last year.
THE GUARDIAN
-- BRITAIN SEEKS REVISION TO IMF RULE ON CAPITAL FLOWS

Britain yesterday called for a revision of the IMF's charter to give the fund an exclusive right to promote capital flows and dismantle controls. Britain believes the free movement of capital gives countries with investment opportunities access to new sources of funds. The US supports Britain's stand, but developing countries are wary.
-- C&W VALUED AT 4.5 BILLION STG AS TRADING STARTS

Shares in Cable & Wireless Communications started trading yesterday with the group valued at just under 4.5 billion stg. Shares opened in London and New York at 300p, peaking at 309p before slipping to 299.5p. The group is the result of the merger between Mercury Communications, Nynex CableComms, Bell Cablemedia and Videotron.
-- UK BANK CHIEFS 'COULD FACE JAIL OVER CRIME CASH'

City solicitors Titmuss Sainer Dechert and the Manhattan district attorney's office warned yesterday that British bank chairmen and managing directors faced the prospect of jail terms over money laundering. A survey by Titmuss showed a dearth of training of bank officers over money laundering. The Manhattan attorney, speaking at a Titmuss seminar, refused to apologise for earlier suggestions that New York banks were routing illicit deals through London because of Wall Street's tougher approach.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- G7 WARNING FAILS TO DAMPEN THE RISING DOLLAR

Despite feeling from the G7 nations that its rise must be curtailed, the dollar continued to rise, reaching its highest level against the yen and the Deutschmark for several years before dropping slightly. Currency traders took the G7's bland warning to suggest little danger of central bank intervention to halt the dollar's constant rise.
-- COMMISSIONER SAYS EMU ON COURSE

Yves-Thibault de Silguy, European Commissioner responsible for single currency, said in Washington that monetary union remained on course. His comments were in response to IMF warnings about the danger of delay to currency markets. He said he had no fears that France and Germany would fail to qualify.
-- ENTERPRISE UNVEILS 100 MILLION STG SWAP

Enterprise Oil Plc yesterday announced an asset swap with British Petroleum Co Plc. The move will strengthen its North Sea presence and end its involvement in the British Gas GAS.L take-or-pay affair. BP will exchange its 43 percent interest in the Pierce field for Enterprise's interests in the Amethyst and Ravenspurn North gas fields.
